subject: general
question: Suez canal is an artificial waterway that connects which of the following seas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Suez Canal is an artificial sea-level waterway in Egypt, connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea through the Isthmus of Suez.
 
• It was opened for navigation on November 17, 1869, and has since become one of the world's most important waterways, facilitating maritime trade between Europe and Asia.
 
• The canal allows ships to travel between Europe and South Asia without navigating around Africa, significantly reducing the sea voyage distance.
 
• The Suez Canal is approximately 193 kilometers (120 miles) long, and it has no locks because it is at sea level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Artificial Waterway:**

 
 
• An artificial waterway or canal is a man-made channel constructed to allow the passage of boats or ships inland or to convey water for irrigation.
 
• Canals are used for transportation, irrigation, water supply, or drainage.
 
 
 
• **Isthmus of Suez:**
 
 
• The Isthmus of Suez is the narrow land bridge that connects Africa and Asia.
 
• The Suez Canal cuts through this isthmus, allowing direct maritime travel between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.
 
 
 
• **Maritime Trade:**
 
 
• Maritime trade involves the transport of goods and services across seas and oceans.
 
• It is a critical component of global trade, with a significant portion of international trade being carried out by sea.
 
 
 
• **Locks:**
 
 
• Locks are devices used for raising and lowering boats between stretches of water of different levels on rivers and canal waterways.
 
• They are essential in canals that have significant elevation changes; however, the Suez Canal does not require locks because it is at sea level.
